heard: Saturn has two moons locked in a constant orbital dance. Their orbital paths differ by only 50 kilometers. That tiny gap should cause a violent collision. Instead, as the inner moon catches up, gravity forces a swap. They pass between 10,000 and 15,000 kilometers apart. Every four years, they trade inner and outer positions. Janus is four times more massive, shifting Epimetheus four times more. Voyager 1 confirmed this unique dance in 1980, making this the solar system's only known orbital swap.
